requiredClientIdentifiers.label: NIP (Numer Identyfikacji Podatkowej)
requiredClientIdentifiers.why: FA(3) requires the buyer's NIP in the Podmiot2/DaneIdentyfikacyjne block (`formats/national/fa3-provider.ts` reads `getIdentifier(client, 'VAT')`, stripped of any leading two-letter country prefix) — a government client (a Jednostki Samorządu Terytorialnego/JST or a central body) with no NIP on file cannot be built into a FA(3) document at all. ksef.podatki.gov.pl's own JST page confirms this is not a formality: "Podatnicy krajowi posiadający NIP, odbierają faktury przy użyciu systemu (czyli elektronicznie)" ("Domestic taxpayers WITH a NIP receive invoices using the system [KSeF], i.e. electronically") — the NIP is what makes a Polish public body a KSeF-addressable recipient at all.

provenance.sourceText: eInvoicing Country Factsheet — Poland (European Commission, Digital Building Blocks, eInvoicing space, page last updated 14 Aug 2025): "Businesses will use KSeF for B2B e-Invoices, while B2G transactions can be processed through either KSeF or PEF" — both platforms operate "within the OpenPeppol network". Separately, on the Polish Ministry of Finance's own KSeF portal (ksef.podatki.gov.pl/jednostki-samorzadu-terytorialnego-jst/, the page dedicated to local government units): "Podatnicy krajowi posiadający NIP, odbierają faktury przy użyciu systemu (czyli elektronicznie)" — domestic NIP-holding taxpayers, which includes JST public bodies, receive their invoices through KSeF. The same official page lists the phased mandatory rollout: "1 lutego 2026", "1 kwietnia 2026" (with a 10,000 PLN/month threshold exemption), the transitional period for certain exemptions (simplified invoices, cash-register receipts) ending "31 grudnia 2026", and full mandatory compliance from "1 stycznia 2027".

rule.notes: READ DIRECTLY on 2026-09-02, TWO CONVERGING SOURCES: (1) ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467108896/eInvoicing+in+Poland (the European Commission's own official country factsheet); (2) ksef.podatki.gov.pl (the Polish Ministry of Finance's own KSeF portal), in particular its page dedicated to local government units (JST), ksef.podatki.gov.pl/jednostki-samorzadu-terytorialnego-jst/ — reached after two HTTP 301 redirects (podatki.gov.pl/ksef/ → podatki.gov.pl/ksef → ksef.podatki.gov.pl), all followed and read, never guessed. DECISION ON THE CHANNEL — SETTLED BY READING, NOT BY THE MOST OBVIOUS OPTION: the Commission's factsheet documents TWO possible Polish B2G channels, KSeF AND PEF (Platforma Elektronicznego Fakturowania) — PEF having "adopted the Peppol BIS standard and incorporated Polish-specific requirements" then "developed additional extensions to the e-Invoicing standard... approved by OpenPeppol". This rule deliberately chooses KSeF, NOT PEF/Peppol, for a reason of REAL DELIVERABILITY, not preference: PEF's Polish extension (the CIUS/Poland-specific Peppol extensions, approved by OpenPeppol but specific to it) is NOT vendored in this repository — no `formats/*-provider.ts` builds it — whereas KSeF AND its national FA(3) format (`formats/national/fa3-provider.ts`, judged against the official vendored XSD `vendored/pl/schemat_FA3.xsd`, never against an unsuited generic EN 16931 Schematron) are ALREADY implemented and PROVEN LIVE (see the session's own memory: "KSeF channel proven end-to-end, real CLEARED + ksefNumber, 2026-06-28") — sending generic Peppol BIS to PEF would contradict the rule as read (PEF requires the Polish-specific extensions, never bare Peppol BIS), exactly the case this task's own instructions ask to avoid; KSeF, conversely, IS a channel the same factsheet states is usable for B2G ("B2G transactions can be processed through either KSeF or PEF"), and its FA(3) format is the Polish national format itself, never a generic substitute. `transportId: "ksef"` and `formatSyntax: "fa3"` therefore reference building blocks that ACTUALLY exist and are already proven, not a bet. DISTINCTION FROM `channel-policy/data/pl.json` (pre-existing, not modified by this task): that file encodes a DIFFERENT axis — the mandate for the Polish SELLER's OWN country, for EVERY invoice it issues (`requirement: "suggested"`, provenance `unverified`, for lack of as clean a citation as this one at the time); THIS rule encodes the B2G axis — the government CLIENT's country, regardless of the seller's own country — and carries ITS OWN `legal` provenance, independently sourced today (two direct readings, never carried over from channel-policy/pl.json's own note, which itself remains unverified by this task). HONEST LIMIT ON THE TIMELINE: as of the reading date (2026-09-02), KSeF's mandatory rollout is under way but NOT COMPLETE (milestones read: 1 February 2026, 1 April 2026 with an exemption under 10,000 PLN/month, the transitional period for certain exemptions ending 31 December 2026, full compliance from 1 January 2027) — this rule asserts that KSeF IS the recognized Polish B2G channel, never that EVERY send through it is today legally forced for EVERY company size; unlike `channel-policy/schema.ts`, the `b2g-routing/schema.ts` format in any case has NO temporal field (`mandatedFrom`) to grade this — see `schema.ts`'s own header, a B2G rule is a single rule, not dated. NO `requiredDocumentFields` is added: FA(3) carries no B2G-specific field requirement beyond the NIP already covered by `requiredClientIdentifiers` above.
